findings.claim: AUTH_ELEVATION_WINDOW_SECONDS is parsed with Number.parseInt but is never added to RootConfigurationSchema, unlike its neighbour AUTH_STATE_TTL_MILLISECONDS which is validated with z.coerce.number().int().min(1_000).optional(). A bad value like "30m" becomes NaN, and since ageSeconds <= NaN is always false, every OIDC admin gets 403 elevation_required on every gated route when the flag is on, while the app still boots normally; zero or negative values are also accepted without error.
The new mfaStepUp flag mapping lacks a comment naming who owns the flag and under what condition it should be removed, which the feature-flag documentation requires.

The "Guards and Decorators" section lists AuthGuard, OptionalAuthGuard and OidcAuthRateLimitGuard but omits the new ElevationGuard, its SIWE exemption, and the elevation_required contract that clients rely on.

The "Other Auth Config" table is missing the new AUTH_ELEVATION_WINDOW_SECONDS variable, and the ?elevate=true query parameter on authorize plus the amr check in the callback are not documented anywhere.

oidcPayload and siwePayload are constructed as hand-written object literals instead of using the existing oidcAuthPayloadDtoBuilder() and siweAuthPayloadDtoBuilder() builders already used elsewhere in this PR (auth-payload.entity.spec.ts and elevation.integration.spec.ts), which is inconsistent with the established test convention.

The test for the exact window edge (300 seconds) builds its timestamp with Date.now(), and since hasFreshMfa calls Date.now() again separately, a clock crossing a second boundary between the two calls can push the age to 301, causing the "fresh" assertion to fail intermittently.

The "very edge of the window" test has the same intermittent failure risk as the auth-payload.entity.spec.ts edge case, since it relies on two separate Date.now() calls instead of a frozen clock; other specs in the codebase (oidc-auth.service.spec.ts:48) already use vi.useFakeTimers() and vi.setSystemTime() to avoid this.

buildAuth0Token(amr) as never uses a type cast to satisfy a mock signature, hiding type drift, whereas the other cases in the same file (lines 93, 140, 182) pass a typed object directly into mockResolvedValue without a cast; giving buildAuth0Token the repository's actual return type (Auth0Token) instead of Record<string, unknown> would remove the need for the cast.

signedPayload() reads authRepositoryMock.signToken.mock.calls[0][0] as Record<string, unknown> and indexes into mock.calls directly (used by assertions from lines 428–469), instead of using expect(...).toHaveBeenCalledWith(expect.objectContaining(...)) style assertions, including expect.not.objectContaining for cases where the stamp should be absent.

The describe.each(GATED_ROUTES) block (lines 272–309) repeats five cases per gated route (never-MFA, expired, fresh, SIWE-exempt, unauthenticated), but the expired, fresh, and SIWE cases duplicate coverage already present in elevation.guard.spec.ts; per route it would suffice to keep one rejection test and one allow test, leaving the window and SIWE branches to the unit tests.
